title: SEBI Clarifies Rules for Private Share Transfers in Unlisted Companies
summary: Prevents illegal public offerings disguised as private secondary share sales.

blocks.content: Prevents illegal public offerings disguised as private secondary share sales.

items: Secondary transfer of unlisted company shares by an existing shareholder to **≤200 buyers in a FY** is **NOT** treated as a public issue.
Contractual rights like **Right of First Refusal (ROFR)** can be honored.
Exceeding **200 buyers per FY** automatically converts the transaction into a **Deemed Public Issue**.

blocks.title: Static Background & GK Context
blocks.summary: SEBI established 1988, statutory powers in 1992 via SEBI Act, 1992 | HQ: Mumbai.

blocks.title: Exam Trap & Statutory Distinction
blocks.content: 200 buyers limit per FY for secondary unlisted share deals vs 200 private placement limit under Sec 42 Companies Act 2013.

blocks.quote:
Interview Focus Question: "Why did SEBI set a 200-buyer cap per FY for secondary unlisted share deals?"
💡 **Model Answer: Prevents unlisted companies from conducting backdoor public issues without fulfilling prospectus disclosure rules.**
blocks.author: Banking & Regulatory Board Panel
